request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export claims (CSV)" button that downloads the claims as a CSV file, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The change is one new file, `src/main/frontend/features/claims/export.slot.tsx`. It sits in the same panel area as the people export, just after it, and works the same way: the file is built in the browser from data the screen already has, so nothing changed on the server, in the stored data or in the audit file.

- **Columns:** the header line is `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`.
- **Order:** people come in list order, retired people included. Each person's claims are oldest first, which is just the on-screen list (newest first) reversed.
- **Values:** each figure uses the same calculation as the claim's row on screen. That means an empty number or period stays empty, and a due that can't be worked out shows `n/a`.
- **Quoting and line ends:** same as the people export. A value is wrapped in double quotes when it holds a comma, a quote or a line break, and every line ends with `\n`.

The quoting helper is now copied in both export files rather than shared. I left it that way to keep the change small.
